The lead is held at chemical potential $\mu$ and inverse temperature $\beta>0$; its occupation is
the Fermi function $n_F(\omega) = 1/(e^{\beta(\omega-\mu)}+1)$. For a level of width $\Gamma>0$ the
occupation-weighted propagator integrates to
\begin{equation}
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} d\omega\, \frac{n_F(\omega)}{(\omega-\epsilon)^2+\Gamma^2} = \frac{\pi}{2\Gamma} - \frac{1}{2i\Gamma}\left[\psi\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\beta(\Gamma+i\epsilon)}{2\pi}\right)-\psi\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\beta(\Gamma-i\epsilon)}{2\pi}\right)\right] .
\label{eq:occ}
\end{equation}
